name: libass
notes: 2026-11-01: Reference ASS/SSA renderer behind FFmpeg's ass and subtitles filters; styled and karaoke-timed burn-in.
2026-11-01: Pin font files; system font fallback breaks reproducibility. May be better recorded as an FFmpeg capability.

evidence.result: C via Homebrew libass 0.17.5: 50 frames 640x360; TOP LEFT and BOTTOM RIGHT events land in their predeclared regions, gaps empty; 3 distinct hashes; repeat and shuffled runs match; coverage 0..255 with 797 partial pixels at 3000 ms; font log names JetBrainsMono-Bold; contact sheet inspected.
evidence.scope: Hand-written ASS, one style with bundled OFL font via ass_set_fonts_dir, two timed events over a solid background, C on macOS arm64; no FFmpeg filter, karaoke, fades or system fonts.

summary: Portable C library that renders Advanced SubStation Alpha subtitles, including styled text and timed events, to video frames. It is commonly consumed through FFmpeg’s ass/subtitles filters or embedded by media applications rather than used as a standalone authoring tool. Strength: mature ASS rendering with shaping and font-provider integration.
use_when: Render an existing ASS/SSA subtitle track through an FFmpeg filter or a native application
Use for ASS-specific subtitle styling and timed events rather than HTML text overlays
avoid_when: Use FFmpeg when the task is a complete transcode and subtitle filter is already available
Use browser typography or SVG when subtitles are authored as scene graphics

assessment.rationale: libass 0.17.5 released 2026-06-24; official project describes the library and build options. ISC licensed. A focused ASS renderer behind FFmpeg and native integrations; font selection and shaping dependencies affect reproducibility.
